governance.note: Inherits every measured lever of the neiso-27 agt-daily keeper unchanged (the daily Algonquin Citygate gas-basis built from real EIA Natural Gas Weekly Update spot prints + Transco Z6 NY daily-basis shape; historic CAMPD unit-level outage windows; EIA-860 cogen BTM CHP host-steam pulled out of the LP; measured F923 per-plant monthly delivered gas under the measured EIA monthly AGT hub-basis overlay; measured EIA-930 net interchange; measured EIA-860 dual-fuel switching at the delivered oil price) and adds three structural inputs, all measured EIA-860/930 quantities that regenerate for a forward year and respond to changed conditions: (1) HYDRO REPIN -- the hydro energy budget is pinned to the measured EIA-930 NG:WAT monthly grid total (--hydro-eia930-monthly), with non-reporting plants back-filled from the 2024 vintage coverage (--hydro-backfill-year 2024) before per-plant shares are applied. This fixes a DATA-VINTAGE error: the 2025 EIA-923 vintage carried only 5 of ~166 NEISO hydro plants (0.09 TWh) so the ~5 TWh of missing zero-MC hydro had been served by marginal gas CC, inflating CC_REGULAR volume and the mean LMP. The repin uses the measured EIA-930 grid total (a real, forward-reproducible market input), NOT model output -- it is not pinned to actuals; the dispatch still chooses when to spend the budget. (2) STORAGE VINTAGE RAMP on for NEISO (now a backcast default alongside CAISO/ERCOT): battery and pumped-storage dispatch caps step up at each unit's EIA-860 Operating Month rather than a flat year-end fleet. (3) COD/RETIREMENT OFF-RAMP for ALL resource classes: renewables (wind/solar), batteries and pumped storage each respect their EIA-860 Planned Retirement month-by-month, mirroring the existing month-precise COD ON-ramp (one shared convention: missing online month -> COD_FALLBACK_MONTH, missing retirement month -> December). No adder/haircut/sigmoid tuned to a price or volume residual; no unit pinned to its observed CEMS generation; no input rescaled so model output lands on actuals. The gas-offer / daily-AGT path is untouched, so the winter scarcity mechanism (gas->oil switching) is preserved.
governance.validation_note: 2025 hydro fix lands as predicted: model hydro 5.11 TWh vs EIA-930 5.12 (was 0.09). The CC_REGULAR over-build is resolved -- 2025 model gas 59.12 TWh vs EIA-930 60.09 (was 61.10, +5.36) -- and the 2025 system mean LMP falls to 67.98 $/MWh vs actual 65.89 (+3.2%, was 78.13 / +18.6%). Winter scarcity preserved: 2025 oil burn 1.39 TWh (vs actual 1.24; neiso-27 was 1.66, so closer not regressed), pumped-storage discharge 0.54 TWh, 2025 price max 258.98 $/MWh. 2023/2024 move only by the real hydro/COD/retire deltas: 2023 hydro 8.70 vs 8.77, gas 54.88, mean LMP 33.63; 2024 hydro 7.33 vs 7.39, gas 58.72, mean LMP 39.04 -- no material swing. The COD/retirement ramp masked 260/304/396 (P1) unit-months offline across 2023/24/25 as units came online and retired mid-year.

exceptions.magnitude: model +1.05 TWh, share -0.4pp vs actual (out of absolute band)
exceptions.reason: Dramatically improved by the hydro repin -- neiso-27 was +5.36 TWh (the run that motivated this task); the ~5 TWh of zero-MC hydro restored to 2025 displaced the bulk of the CC over-build, leaving a +1.05 TWh residual just outside the per-class band. Total 2025 gas is now -0.97 TWh vs actual (59.12 vs 60.09), so the residual is an intra-gas sub-class allocation tilt (CC vs peaker/other), an offer-side item explicitly out of scope here and NOT to be closed by tuning an offer curve to the residual (CLAUDE.md #1/#11).

exceptions.magnitude: model -64.1% (0.75 vs 2.08 TWh; pumped-storage 0.54 vs 1.93, battery 0.21 vs 0.15)
exceptions.reason: A downstream consequence of the CORRECT hydro repin, kept per CLAUDE.md #11 (a structurally-correct measured input stays in even when it makes a residual worse). Restoring the ~5 TWh of measured zero-MC hydro to 2025 flattens the price-spread scarcity that had been over-driving pumped-storage arbitrage, so PS discharge falls 1.14 -> 0.54 TWh (neiso-27 -> neiso-28) further below the actual 1.93. Verified NOT a code artifact of the storage vintage/retirement refactor: NEISO's pumped-storage fleet is old and flat, so the COD/retirement ramp is a confirmed no-op (PS capacity 1865 MW identical ramp on/off, 0 units ramped). The real root cause is under-modeled PS arbitrage / multi-day cycling and reserve value, a separate follow-up item, NOT closable by re-pinning storage to its observed throughput.

Unchanged from neiso-27 and out of scope for this run. The real daily AGT spot reaches ~$27-36/MMBtu on the coldest days, but every gas tranche flagged dual-fuel by EIA-860 is capped at the delivered oil price (~$18/MMBtu), so the cleared LMP tops out near the oil-peaker cost (~$293/MWh, model 2025 max 258.98) and never exceeds $300. The >$300 scarcity hours in the real market come from single-fuel gas bidding the full AGT spot and from ORDC/reserve scarcity pricing, neither fully represented. This is an open structural item for a follow-up (single-fuel gas offer at AGT spot; reserve scarcity), NOT addressed or maskable by the hydro/COD/retirement inputs, and explicitly NOT to be closed by re-tuning the gas input to the residual.
